current_example.title: Example: Differentiating a General Exponential Function Using the Chain Rule

q-11817.name: Question 1
q-11817.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f={e}^{u},\,u=2x+5.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot 2 \\  & =2{e}^{u} \\  & =2{e}^{2x+5}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-11817.html:
Question 1
?

Given that f(x)=e2x+5, find dfdx.

a
2xe2x+5
b
e2x+52
c
e2x+5
d
2e2x+5
e
(2x+5)e2x+5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as the composite function f=eu,u=2x+5.

Differentiating gives

dfdu=eu,dudx=2.

We now apply the chain rule, and get

dfdx=dfdu⋅dudx=eu⋅2=2eu=2e2x+5.

q-340496.name: Question 2
q-340496.worked_solution:
First, we express $y={e}^{-3x+5}$ as the composite function

$$
y={e}^{u},\,u=-3x+5.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-3.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (-3) \\  & =-3{e}^{u} \\  & =-3{e}^{-3x+5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the sum rule of differentiation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(8x+{e}^{-3x+5}) \\  & =8-3{e}^{-3x+5} \\  & =-3{e}^{-3x+5}+8.\end{aligned}
$$

q-340496.html:
Question 2
?
Calculate f′(x) if f(x)=8x+e−3x+5.
f′(x)=
8−3e−3x+5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we express y=e−3x+5 as the composite function y=eu,u=−3x+5.

Differentiating gives dydu=eu,dudx=−3.

We now apply the chain rule and get dydx=dydu⋅dudx=eu⋅(−3)=−3eu=−3e−3x+5.

Finally, using the sum rule of differentiation, we have dfdx=ddx(8x+e−3x+5)=8−3e−3x+5=−3e−3x+5+8.

q-340954.name: Question 3
q-340954.worked_solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={e}^{u},\,u=-2{x}^{7}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-14{x}^{6}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (-14{x}^{6}) \\  & =-14{x}^{6}{e}^{u} \\  & =-14{x}^{6}{e}^{-2{x}^{7}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(-14{x}^{6}{e}^{-2{x}^{7}})|}_{x=1} \\  & =-14(1)^{6}{e}^{-2(1)^{7}} \\  & =-14{e}^{-2}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express y as the composite function y=eu,u=−2x7.

Differentiating gives dydu=eu,dudx=−14x6.

We now apply the chain rule and get dydx=dydu⋅dudx=eu⋅(−14x6)=−14x6eu=−14x6e−2x7.

Finally, to find the slope m of the tangent to the curve at x=1, we have to evaluate dydx at that point as follows: m=dydx|x=1=(−14x6e−2x7)|x=1=−14(1)6e−2(1)7=−14e−2

q-48629.name: Question 4
q-48629.worked_solution:
First we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f={e}^{u},\,u=8-2{x}^{3}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-6{x}^{2}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot (-6{x}^{2}) \\  & =-6{x}^{2}{e}^{8-2{x}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-340970.name: Question 5
q-340970.worked_solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=2\cdot {5}^{u},\,u=1-3x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=2\cdot {5}^{u}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5),\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-3.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =2\cdot {5}^{u}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)\cdot (-3) \\  & =-6\cdot {5}^{1-3x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=0$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=0} & ={(-6\cdot {5}^{1-3x}\operatorname{ln}⁡5)|}_{x=0} \\  & =-6\cdot {5}^{1-3(0)}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\  & =-6\cdot 5\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\  & =-30\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)\end{aligned}
$$

q-107463.name: Question 6
q-107463.problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y={4}^{2x+1}$ at the point where $x=-1.$
q-107463.worked_solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={4}^{u},\,u=2x+1.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={4}^{u}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4),\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={4}^{u}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)\cdot 2 \\  & =2\cdot {4}^{2x+1}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=-1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point. 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-1} & ={(2\cdot {4}^{2x+1}\operatorname{ln}⁡4)|}_{x=-1} \\  & =2\cdot {4}^{-1}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((4)^{1/2}) \\  & =ln\,(\,\sqrt{4}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2).\end{aligned}
$$

Also, the $y$-value of the point on the curve where $x={x}_{1}=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & ={({4}^{2x+1})|}_{x=-1} \\  & ={4}^{2(-1)+1} \\  & ={4}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-\frac{1}{4} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\cdot (x+1) \\ y-\frac{1}{4} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\,x+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\,x+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

q-107463.html:
Question 6
?

Find the equation of the tangent to the curve y=42x+1 at the point where x=−1.

a
y=ln⁡(2)x+ln⁡(2)+14
b
y=−ln⁡(2)x−ln⁡(2)
c
y=ln⁡(2)x−14
d
y=−ln⁡(2)x−2ln⁡(2)+14
e
y=2ln⁡(2)x−2ln⁡(2)+14
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we express y as the composite function

y=4u,u=2x+1.

Differentiating gives

dydu=4uln⁡(4),dudx=2.

We now apply the chain rule, and get

dydx=dydu⋅dudx=4uln⁡(4)⋅2=2⋅42x+1ln⁡(4).

Now, to find the slope of the tangent to the curve at x=−1, we have to evaluate dydx at that point. dydx|x=−1=(2⋅42x+1ln⁡4)|x=−1=2⋅4−1ln⁡(4)=12ln⁡(4)=ln⁡((4)1/2)=ln(4)=ln⁡(2).

Also, the y-value of the point on the curve where x=x1=−1 is y1=(42x+1)|x=−1=42(−1)+1=4−1=14.

Finally, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

y−y1=m(x−x1)y−14=ln⁡(2)⋅(x+1)y−14=ln⁡(2)x+ln⁡(2)y=ln⁡(2)x+ln⁡(2)+14
